48:Library reality, checked with `python -c import`: torch, tensorflow, hmmlearn, stumpy, ruptures, tslearn, sktime, pyts are absent and nothing may be installed. Present: numpy 2.2, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3, scipy 1.14, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2, shap 0.49, matplotlib 3.9, PIL, pyarrow, psutil. Consequences, stated per study: a gradient-trained 1D-CNN/GRU/Transformer is not possible without a framework (a hand-written numpy CNN is a day of build for no expected gain at n=4.5k); its honest modern substitute is the random-convolutional-kernel transform (ROCKET/MiniRocket) plus a linear probe, which the literature shows matches small CNNs on small time-series benchmarks and which I benchmarked here at 2.1 s per 1,500 windows x 2,000 kernels. Contrastive pretraining (InfoNCE) needs a custom loss, so the self-supervised study uses the ladder PCA -> sklearn MLP autoencoder -> forecast-pretext encoder and reports whether anything beats PCA. Matrix profile, HMM, statistical jump model and Bayesian online change-point detection are all implementable in numpy/numba in under 150 lines each and were timed (FFT distance profile 0.19 s per query over the whole 445k-bar 1m tape; GMM on 90k x 6 in 51 s).
86:**technique.** Latent regime states from per-bar features: a hand-rolled Gaussian HMM (Baum-Welch, causal forward filtering at inference), a statistical jump model (k-means with a jump penalty, online prefix version), a GaussianMixture no-dynamics baseline, and Bayesian online change-point detection (BOCPD) run-length features; all fit on IS bars only.
90:**method.** Per-bar as-of feature vector x_t from fz_v3/<tf>/bars.csv and events.csv: |log return|, (high-low)/atr14, |close-open|/(high-low), log(volume/median volume of the previous 20 bars), events (BOS+CHoCH) in the last 36 bars, CHoCHs since the last BOS at t, range of the last 36 bars / atr14, signed 36-bar return / atr14; features are z-scored with IS statistics. Models: (a) Gaussian HMM with K in {3,4}, diagonal covariance, Baum-Welch 50 iterations in numba, initialised from k-means, fit on IS bars of the training folds; at inference only the forward (filtered) posterior P(s_t | x_<=t) is used; the smoothed posterior is computed too but only as a hindsight diagnostic. (b) Statistical jump model: minimise sum ||x_t - mu_{s_t}||^2 + lambda * 1[s_t != s_{t-1}] by alternating centroid updates and Viterbi DP, lambda from a small grid chosen on CV; the online state is the prefix-DP argmax. (c) sklearn GaussianMixture(K) on the same vectors as the no-dynamics baseline. (d) BOCPD (Adams & MacKay) with a normal-inverse-gamma predictive on 1m/5m log returns and separately on log range, hazard 1/H for H in {60, 240} bars, run-length truncated at 400; features: MAP run length, P(run length < 10), bars since the last MAP reset. At each SETUP bar k the study attaches: P(state = c | x_<=k) for each state, the jump-model state, and the BOCPD features. Analysis: Foundation net and win rate by filtered state and by BOCPD run-length bucket on IS; identify the state with the worst expectancy (the candidate chop state) inside each training fold; gate = skip when P(chop) >= tau (tau grid 0.5..0.9) or run length >= r; evaluate on purged session-blocked CV against H2's rule at matched skip fraction (the HMM must beat the hand rule's kept-vs-skipped difference at the same trade count, else it is not worth its parameters); final model refit on all IS; OOS once. Outputs: state description tables (means per feature), transition matrix, the expectancy-by-state table on IS CV and OOS, the control percentile, and the distilled rule.
100:**novelty.** Markov-switching regimes (Hamilton 1989) and Gaussian HMMs (Rabiner 1989) are classical; the current pieces are statistical jump models for regime detection with an online variant (Bemporad et al. 2018; Nystrup, Kolm & Lindstrom 2020/2021, 'sparse jump models'), Bayesian online change-point detection (Adams & MacKay 2007) as a causal alternative to offline change-point search (ruptures, Truong et al. 2020), and the discipline of separating filtered from smoothed states (the look-ahead trap in regime backtests documented by Nystrup et al.).
166:**novelty.** Matrix profile and MASS (Yeh et al. ICDM 2016; Mueen 2015; STOMP/SCRIMP 2017-2018), motif and discord discovery as the current standard for unsupervised pattern mining in long series; shapelets (Ye & Keogh 2009), learned/random shapelets (Grabocka et al. 2014; Karlsson et al. 2016 random shapelet forests); k-Shape and time-series clustering benchmarks (Paparrizos & Gravano 2015; Javed et al. 2020). The causal prefix-novelty score is a matrix-profile discord applied online.
190:**Judge 1** feasible 2 · rigour 3 · expected value 1 · keep False — fix: Trap: a 16-unit sklearn MLP autoencoder is nonlinear PCA, not a foundation model; 3-4 CPU-hours at 750 MB on a box already carrying another session's build, to confirm the negative the study itself predicts, with 'embedding dimension correlates with a named feature' read as discovery. Fix: do not run; a PCA-16 linear probe (seconds) as a footnote in study 9 if that runs; revisit only with torch and a longer tape.
266:**method.** Score s(x) = 1 - p_win_hat(x) taken from the meta-label study's IS out-of-fold probabilities (the scorecard variant, since the forest cannot live in the lab; the forest's scores are reported as reference). Cross-conformal / CV+ flavour: no separate calibration split is sacrificed (181 winners on 5m IS cannot afford one); within the harness's 12 purged folds, the conformal quantile is computed on the OOF scores of the winners in 11 folds and applied to the 12th, so the IS evaluation is itself out-of-fold. Mondrian by class: q_alpha = the ceil((n_win + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest OOF score among true winners; the prediction set contains 'win' iff s(x) <= q_alpha; gate = skip iff 'win' is not in the set, i.e. p_win_hat(x) < 1 - q_alpha. Guarantee: P(win in set | true winner) >= 1 - alpha, so at most alpha of winners are skipped in expectation; nothing is guaranteed for losers, their recall is measured. Alpha grid {0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30}; the smallest feasible alpha is 1/(n_win + 1) (0.0055 on 5m IS). Time taxonomy: class x time bin with three bins fixed in advance (09:15-10:29, 10:30-12:59, 13:00-15:19; the IS hour profile shows morning losses and afternoon gains); feasibility stated from winner counts per bin (5m IS: 16-39 winners per hour, so per-bin guarantees only for alpha >= 0.1; on 1m roughly 4-5x more). Robustness: |net|-weighted coverage (share of winners' gross net kept) reported next to count coverage, because the guarantee is per SETUP, not per rupee. Evaluation on IS-OOF per alpha: skip rate, winner coverage, loser recall, kept-vs-skipped expectancy and permutation p, control percentile (fz_report.random_control), top-decile-winner coverage; alpha chosen on IS by the pre-registered rule 'largest loser recall subject to winner coverage >= 0.9 and kept-vs-skipped difference > 0'. Exchangeability check: coverage per IS year and against the regime study's break tests. ACI variant (Gibbs and Candes): alpha_t+1 = alpha_t + gamma (alpha - err_t), gamma in {0.005, 0.01}, run sequentially over IS in time order, then continued into OOS from IS's final state without re-tuning, to see whether an online alpha keeps coverage under drift. OOS once: the frozen (alpha, taxonomy, thresholds) and the frozen ACI state, same table.
---
33:   - **Trade journal.** One row per Foundation SETUP (taken or skipped) and per closed trade: timestamp, direction, the full feature vector at the decision bar (card fields, regime, volume, level context, time), the policy's decision and its stated reason, the policy's state id (which model / which update it was made with), fill, exit reason, MFE / MAE, pts, gross, costs, net, R-multiple, and the running book (equity, drawdown, rolling profit factor). This journal is the training set of the online learner and the audit trail of every decision. In the lab build it is a table the strategy writes (`fz_journal.csv` or a `journal` block in the results), never a side effect hidden in code.
34:   - **Learning after each trade (online / walk-forward).** The policy used at trade t is fitted only on journal rows of trades closed before t (strictly causal; anchored or rolling window as a config key), and is refitted after every closed trade (or every k trades, k a key). Actions: take / skip and position size (lots, bounded by a money-management rule such as fractional Kelly on the calibrated win probability and the expected R, with a maximum lots key and a daily loss stop key). Reward: net P&L per trade with the objective reported as net, profit factor (gross wins / gross losses), max drawdown and the kept-vs-skipped expectancy; because profit factor is not additive, the learner optimises a per-trade surrogate (net, or net with an asymmetric loss penalty) and the policy is *selected* on walk-forward profit factor. Candidate learners, all to be run and compared: contextual bandits with exploration (LinUCB / Thompson sampling on a logistic or tree-embedded model), online gradient-boosted refits, and an offline-RL exit policy (fitted Q-iteration / conservative Q-learning over bar-by-bar in-trade states with doubly-robust off-policy evaluation). Evaluate the whole walk-forward path on IS (learning curve: after how many trades does the policy beat "take everything" and the random control?) and then once on OOS with the learner continuing to update through OOS exactly as it would live. Compare against the static IS-fitted model and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate.
37:6. **Coordination with the other lab session ("Buy only").** Their strategies 19-24 (`rl.py`, `entry_rule rl_v1`) are a contextual bandit (Bayesian linear regression per action, Thompson sampling) that chooses, at each Foundation SETUP, skip or an exit profile x stop x lots from Foundation-side features, with full-information updates in exit-time order, learning from Oct 2021 onward. FZ v3 does not duplicate that: v3 decides take / skip from room, regime, volume, level and time context with its own journal and online learner; for the exit / size stage compose with `rl.py` where it exists (or a config-level reference to it) rather than building a second bandit, and say so in the strategy files. ST15-ST18 are their positional exit variants; do not touch strategies 9-12 and 15-24.

56:- Lens and framing. Foundation is the primary model: it fixes side, entry bar and exit rule for every SETUP, and (decisively) its outcome is observed for every SETUP in the data, taken or not. So the take/skip/size decision at the SETUP bar is a one-step problem with full-information feedback: it is supervised meta-labelling in Lopez de Prado's sense, not a bandit (no off-policy correction is needed because the counterfactual is in the table) and not sequential RL (no position overlap: 0 of 1,003 Foundation trades overlap on 5m, by construction the next SETUP needs the CHoCH that exits the previous trade). Everything proposed below descends from that framing: the labels and weights (AFML ch. 3-4), the validation harness (ch. 7, 11-14), importance with substitution effects removed (ch. 8; MLAM ch. 6), calibrated sizing (ch. 10), conformal sets for the skip decision (Vovk; Angelopoulos and Bates), and break/explosiveness statistics as regime features (ch. 17). Sample-size reality drives the design: on 5m IS there are 823 SETUPs and 181 winners; the engine-label net has std 10,271 INR (holds run to 70 sessions because the engine has no square-off), so a kept-vs-skipped expectancy difference below about 1,400 INR per trade (400 vs 400 split, 5% two-sided) is undetectable on that label. The intraday label (exit forced at the entry session's 15:25 bar, the lab's ST1/ST2 book) is therefore the primary label in every study; the top decile of winners carries 46% of gross wins (win mean +10,878, loss mean -3,429), so every gate is judged on |net|-weighted winner recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy plus the session-matched random control, never on accuracy or net alone (a gate that trades less always saves costs). Data facts the studies rely on: the 5-minute table at scratchpad/fz_v3/5minute (features.parquet, 186 columns, 143 as-of; 97 numeric with 114 pairs |rho| > 0.9; causality verified by the truncated build), the 1-minute table not yet landed (scripts 01-03 only) but promised with the same column contract (a few thousand SETUPs). Box: 4 logical cores, 7.9 GB RAM with about 1.2 GB free beside the other session's 1.1 GB lab process; every study is a single process under 500 MB and 25 CPU-minutes per timeframe, at most two at a time, no pip installs (numpy 2.2.6, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.14.1, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, numba 0.65, joblib; statsmodels/mapie/mlfinlab/lightgbm/torch absent, so ADF, CUSUM, FFD, conformal and PBO are hand-coded in numpy, all short). Order and dependencies: the harness (study 2) first because every other study and H1-H5 consume its splitter and trials ledger; then meta-labelling (1) which also hands H5 its labels, weights, OOF probabilities and splitter instead of a second gradient-boosting run; importance (3) and regime (6) can run in parallel with (1) since they only need the splitter; conformal (4) and sizing (5) consume (1)'s OOF file and are cheap. Deliberately left out with reasons: sequential bootstrap (uniqueness is 1 by construction for Foundation labels; only the triple-barrier variants with vertical barriers overlap and those get the concurrency weights inside study 1); HRP / portfolio construction (one instrument); deep sequence models and transformers (1k-5k labels, no GPU, and nothing to distil into 8 rules); sequential RL (one-step decision with the counterfactual observed); generative AI in the LLM sense (no standing in the canon at this sample size; the only generative element the canon endorses here is the CPCV path distribution and the stationary block bootstrap of sessions in study 2, which is what gives the confidence intervals). OOS discipline shared by all six: candidate configs and the exact scoring scripts are frozen to JSON with a sha before any OOS row is read; the harness pre-registers the go/no-go rule (PBO <= 0.2, CPCV 5th-percentile kept-vs-skipped difference > 0, deflated-Sharpe p < 0.1, at most three candidates across all lenses get the one OOS look); the frozen ST7/ST8 gate is always one of the comparators; ST13/ST14 must carry square_off "15:25" so that the traded book matches the label the gate was learned on.
58:- Why this lens splits the problem the way it does. (1) The take/skip choice at a Foundation SETUP is a contextual bandit with FULL information: Foundation took every SETUP, so the reward of "take" (fnd_net, 1m: 5,326 rows, 5m: 1,012 rows) is logged for every context, and the reward of "skip" is exactly 0 by definition. There is no unobserved arm, hence no propensity model, no inverse-propensity weighting and no doubly-robust correction: the off-policy value of ANY gate pi is computed exactly as sum over SETUPs of pi(x)*net(x). The only statistical problem is generalisation from a few thousand contexts, so the right tools are cost-sensitive policy learning (value-maximising policy trees, cost-proportionate weighting) and honest selection, not bandit exploration. (2) Sequential RL is genuinely justified only where today's action changes which future rewards remain reachable: the in-trade exit (hold/exit/partial each bar; 1m IS has ~186k intraday bar-steps inside positions, ~800k once trajectories are extended to the 15:25 square-off) and, at session level, whether to keep trading today. On a price-taker's tape the dynamics are exogenous (an Exo-MDP): any exit policy can be replayed exactly and the hindsight-optimal exit is computable per trade, so OPE (DR/MAGIC) is not the bottleneck; generalisation and multiplicity are. Deep offline RL (CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer) and neural generators (TimeGAN, diffusion) are not runnable here (no torch) and would be badly over-parameterised for 4.5k trajectories anyway; the studies say so and use the closest feasible analogues (pessimistic tree-ensemble FQI, hindsight-imitation, GMM-Markov and session-bootstrap tapes). (3) Sizing is a downstream Kelly problem that only exists once a positive-conditional-edge region is found; the raw book (win rate 15%, mean -922 INR) has negative Kelly, and the study is written to return "0 lots" honestly. (4) Costs are 1,050-1,120 INR per trade and the median 1m trade moves 9 pts, so a gate that trades less always raises net by the saved costs: every study judges on kept-vs-skipped expectancy, the session-matched random control at the same per-session position count (fz_report.random_control), the permutation p, and (new here) the multiplicity-adjusted SPA/PBO from session-block resampling. (5) Leakage discipline is shared: features from the as-of columns only (prefixes fnd_, fwd_, fzpos_, st7_ POST columns, swings.broken_final, events.window_end/end, zones/visits final-state fields are excluded), contiguous session-block CV with purge (drop training trades whose exit falls in the test block) and a 2-session embargo, OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) touched once per study at the end; the 5-minute engine trades are re-cut at 15:25 from bars because the build carries no square-off (358 of 1,012 held overnight). Priority order: the gate (1), the exit policy (2), then the robustness/multiplicity certificate that must pass before any key ships (3), the certified operating point (4), sizing (5), the session-stop rule (6). Compute: every study fits in one process under 1 GB; the two heavy jobs (1m FQI ensemble, 1m synthetic tapes) must not run concurrently with each other because each peaks near 900 MB.
262:**technique.** Class-conditional (Mondrian) cross-conformal prediction on the meta-model's nonconformity score, with the skip decision defined as 'win is not in the prediction set', a Mondrian taxonomy by class x time bin for the user's 'different for different time', and Adaptive Conformal Inference for drift in the live/walk-forward version.
326:### decision-making-1-fullinfo-bandit-policy-tree-gate (priority 1)
328:**technique.** Offline contextual bandit with full-information rewards, solved as cost-sensitive policy learning: value-maximising depth-limited policy trees (Athey-Wager / Zhou-Athey-Wager) and cost-proportionate weighted gradient boosting, with the policy value computed exactly (direct method, no IPS) and distilled to a rule list
342:**novelty.** Athey & Wager 2021 (Policy learning with observational data) and Zhou, Athey & Wager 2023 (Offline multi-action policy learning: exact depth-limited policy trees) supply the value-maximising tree; Zadrozny, Langford & Abe 2003 (cost-proportionate example weighting) and Beygelzimer & Langford 2009 (offset tree) are the bandit-to-classification reductions, which become exact here because the reward of both arms is known (Dudik, Langford & Li 2011's doubly-robust estimator collapses to the direct method). Distillation follows Bastani, Kim & Bastani 2018 (policy extraction into decision trees). This differs from H5 in the objective: H5 fits win/loss; this maximises INR value with the skip reward pinned at 0 and the costs inside the reward.
430:**novelty.** Kelly 1956 and Thorp 2006 (growth-optimal sizing); MacLean, Thorp & Ziemba 2010 (fractional Kelly and its risk-growth trade-off); Busseti, Ryu & Boyd 2016 (risk-constrained Kelly gambling with a drawdown constraint as a convex problem); Baker & McHale 2013 (Kelly under parameter uncertainty, shrinkage). Sizing is treated as a policy downstream of a calibrated bandit value, not as a standalone optimisation, which is what keeps it from amplifying an overfit gate.

"""Evaluate gates on a synthetic null tape's own feature table (study null_tapes_drift; DESIGN_PANEL decision-making-3 (c)).

A tape folder is what build.py --path <tape.csv> --out <folder> wrote: features.parquet, trades.parquet, sessions.parquet,
bars.parquet, events.parquet, setups.parquet, meta.json. Nothing here touches OUT/ledger: tape results stay in the study
folder (the ledger is for the real tape only).

    import tapes
    T = tapes.load_tape(folder)                       # a harness.Table over the tape's L1 units (all rows are IS by construction)
    res = tapes.evaluate_rule_list(folder, rules)     # rules: a rule-list JSON (grammar below) -> kept-vs-skipped diff, control pct, ...
    res = tapes.evaluate_keep(T, keep_mask, tag)      # any boolean keep mask through harness.metrics (2,000-draw controls)
    h = tapes.tape_health(folder)                     # the engine-health check of one tape (lock-out share, SETUP rate vs real, healthy flag)
    tapes.tape_folders(tf, gen)                       # the CERTIFICATE tape set: the first DESIGN_N healthy tapes per generator (healthy=False: every tape built)
    tapes.null_tape_check(real_diff, tf, rules)       # the pass rule of FINDINGS section 7 as go_no_go-shaped items

Rule-list grammar (the one the LLM-hypothesis study uses, rules_round0.json): a list of rules, each
    {"if": [[column, op, value], ...] (at most 3 comparisons, conjunction), "then": "skip"}
over as-of columns of features.parquet; ops >=, >, <=, <, ==, !=, in, not_in. A SETUP is skipped when ANY rule fires
(disjunction of conjunctions); NaN never satisfies a comparison. A dict {"rules": [...]} or {"minute": [...], "5minute": [...]}
is accepted too (the timeframe list is picked by the tape's tf). A rule may carry "then": "keep" — then the listed rules are
the KEEP set (a SETUP is kept when any keep rule fires); mixing keep and skip rules in one list is refused.

Refused columns (PermissionError): label columns (harness.LABEL_PREFIX), harness.NOT_FEATURES (fz_traded, raw prices, ids), and
the calendar proxies drift.py found (|Spearman rho| >= 0.9 with session_idx: `n_events_asof`, `sl`; read from drift.json,
TIME_PROXIES_FALLBACK when the file is missing). A rule on a time proxy is a calendar rule, not a market rule (FINDINGS section 6).

Engine health of a tape (repair round): on a driftless random-walk tape the engine's protected level can freeze — the anchored
AVWAP of the last flip lags a long one-directional walk, no new swing qualifies as a protected-level candidate (engine.qualifies:
a low below / a high above that AVWAP), `prot` stays at the last candidate and a CHoCH (a close beyond `prot` against the trend)
becomes unreachable while BOS continues. Sessions inside a frozen-`prot`, CHoCH-free run longer than the real tape's longest such
run (68 / 69 sessions on 5minute / minute) are counted as dead; a tape is HEALTHY when its dead share is < HEALTH["dead_share_max"]
(0.2) AND its SETUP rate is >= HEALTH["setup_rate_ratio_min"] (1/3) x the real tape's. The health flag never reads a label or a
gate statistic. The certificate (null_distributions.json `gates`, FINDINGS section 4) is read on the first DESIGN_N healthy
tapes per generator (by seed index k); the sets with the locked tapes are published beside it (`gates_all_original`,
`gates_healthy_original`).

How a candidate is evaluated on the tapes later: for every tape folder of tape_folders(tf, gen) (the certificate set),
evaluate_rule_list(folder, rules) gives the tape's diff and control percentile; the candidate's real-tape diff (its ledger row)
is compared with the p95 of the tape diffs per generator: it passes the null-tape check when its real-tape diff is above the
GMM-Markov p95 AND above the segment p95, and its session-bootstrap diffs are of the same sign as the real one in at least 75%
of the certificate session tapes (null_tape_check does exactly this; see FINDINGS.md section 7).
"""
import os, sys, json, glob
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
if OUT not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, OUT)
import harness as H                                                     # noqa: E402

MECHANICAL_GATES = {
    "frozen_st7_st8": "keep = fz_traded (the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as traded on the tape)",
    "choch2_skip": "skip when n_choch_since_bos >= 2 (mechanical reference gate 1: fixed in tapes.py before any tape was scored; a reference point, not a candidate; BRIEF H2 names the family without k)",
    "sl_above_median_skip": "skip when sl_dist_atr > the tape's own IS median of sl_dist_atr (mechanical reference gate 2: fixed in tapes.py before any tape was scored; a reference point, not a candidate)",
}
DESIGN_N = {"5minute": 20, "minute": 8}                                # tapes per generator the design fixes (DESIGN_PANEL (c), Judge 1 / 2)
HEALTH = dict(dead_share_max=0.2, setup_rate_ratio_min=1.0 / 3.0)    # per-tape poor-null rule (repair round)
TIME_PROXIES_FALLBACK = ("n_events_asof", "sl")                         # drift.py's calendar proxies, used when drift.json is absent
PASS_RULE = dict(session_same_sign_min=0.75)                           # FINDINGS section 7


def load_tape(folder, label="L1"):
    """harness.load for a tape folder: the L1 units (traded, l1_taken) as a harness.Table."""
    F = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(folder, "features.parquet"))
    TR = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(folder, "trades.parquet")).set_index("entry_i")
    S = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(folder, "sessions.parquet"))
    tf = json.load(open(os.path.join(folder, "meta.json")))["timeframe"]
    F = F[F.traded.astype(bool)]
    if label == "L1": F = F[F.l1_taken.astype(bool)]
    F = F.sort_values("setup_i").reset_index(drop=True)
    TR = TR.loc[F.setup_i.to_numpy()].reset_index()
    return H.Table(tf, label, F, TR, S)


def evaluate_keep(T, keep, tag, controls=True, draws=H.CONTROL_DRAWS):
    """Kept-vs-skipped metrics of a keep mask over the tape's IS rows (every tape row is IS), through harness.metrics."""
    rows = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
    m = H.metrics(T, np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool), rows, tag, controls=controls, draws=draws)
    return m

70	class Table:
71	    """One row per unit (a Foundation SETUP taken under the label's book), IS rows first in time order then OOS."""
72	
73	    def __init__(self, tf, label, F, TR, sessions):
74	        self.tf, self.label, self.F, self.TR, self.sessions = tf, label, F, TR, sessions
75	        self.n = len(F)
76	        self.setup_i = F.setup_i.to_numpy()
77	        self.entry_bar = self.setup_i
78	        self.session = F.session_idx.to_numpy()
79	        self.day = F.date.astype(str).to_numpy()
80	        self.is_mask = (F.split.astype(str) == "IS").to_numpy()
81	        self.oos_mask = ~self.is_mask
82	        pre = "l1_" if label == "L1" else "fnd_"
83	        self.net = F[pre + "net_inr"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
84	        self.pts = F[pre + "pts"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
85	        self.exit_bar = F[pre + "exit_i"].to_numpy(dtype=float).astype(int)
86	        self.win = self.net > 0
87	        self.entry_px = TR.entry_px.to_numpy(dtype=float); self.exit_px = TR[pre + "exit_px" if label == "L1" else "exit_px"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
88	        self.up = (F.dir.astype(str) == "up").to_numpy()
89	        self.net_slip = {s: self._net_at_slip(s) for s in (3.0, 5.0, 8.0)}
90	        assert np.allclose(self.net_slip[5.0], self.net, atol=0.02), "slippage 5 must reproduce the label's net"
91	        # 12 contiguous blocks of IS sessions (all IS sessions, active or not, so the blocks are time-contiguous)
92	        is_sess = sessions[sessions.split.astype(str) == "IS"].session_idx.to_numpy()
93	        edges = np.linspace(0, len(is_sess), N_BLOCKS + 1).round().astype(int)
94	        self.block_sessions = [is_sess[edges[b]:edges[b + 1]] for b in range(N_BLOCKS)]
95	        sess2block = {int(s): b for b in range(N_BLOCKS) for s in self.block_sessions[b]}
96	        self.block = np.array([sess2block.get(int(s), -1) for s in self.session])
97	        first_bar = dict(zip(sessions.session_idx, sessions.first_bar)); last_bar = dict(zip(sessions.session_idx, sessions.last_bar))
98	        self.block_range = [(int(first_bar[int(bs[0])]), int(last_bar[int(bs[-1])])) for bs in self.block_sessions]
99	        self.block_embargo = [set(int(s) for s in is_sess[edges[b + 1]:edges[b + 1] + EMBARGO_SESSIONS]) for b in range(N_BLOCKS)]
100	        self.active_sessions = np.array(sorted(set(self.session[self.is_mask].tolist())))
101	        self._asof = None
102	
103	    def _net_at_slip(self, s):
104	        out = np.empty(self.n)
105	        for i in range(self.n):
106	            e, x = self.entry_px[i], self.exit_px[i]
107	            if self.up[i]: buy, sell = e + s, x - s
108	            else: sell, buy = e - s, x + s
109	            out[i] = (sell - buy) * LOT - lab.trade_charges(CS, buy, sell, LOT)["total"]
110	        return out
111	
112	    def asof_columns(self):
113	        """Feature-eligible columns: every column that is not a label, a post-SETUP field, an identity or a raw price / id."""
114	        if self._asof is None:
115	            self._asof = [c for c in self.F.columns if not c.startswith(LABEL_PREFIX) and c not in NOT_FEATURES]
116	        return list(self._asof)
117	
118	    def with_label(self, name, net, exit_bar, pts=None):
119	        """A copy of the table under another label (L2 / L3 ...): net and exit bar per row; the splitter purges by exit_bar."""
120	        T = Table.__new__(Table); T.__dict__.update(self.__dict__)
121	        T.label, T.net, T.exit_bar = name, np.asarray(net, dtype=float), np.asarray(exit_bar).astype(int)
122	        T.pts = np.asarray(pts, dtype=float) if pts is not None else T.pts; T.win = T.net > 0
123	        T.net_slip = {s: self.net_slip[s] + (T.net - self.net) for s in self.net_slip}
124	        return T

139	def design(T, cols=None, max_levels=MAX_LEVELS):
140	    """Numeric design matrix over as-of columns: floats as they are (None -> NaN), booleans 0 / 1, text one-hot (<= max_levels
141	    levels, else dropped). Returns (X DataFrame, {encoded column: source column})."""
142	    cols = list(cols) if cols is not None else T.asof_columns()
143	    out, src = {}, {}
144	    for c in cols:
145	        s = T.F[c]
146	        if pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s): out[c] = s.astype(float).to_numpy(); src[c] = c; continue
147	        if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(s): out[c] = s.to_numpy(dtype=float); src[c] = c; continue
148	        so = s.astype(object)
149	        vals = so.map(lambda z: None if z is None or (isinstance(z, float) and np.isnan(z)) else z)
150	        if all(isinstance(z, (bool, np.bool_)) or z is None for z in vals):
151	            out[c] = vals.map(lambda z: np.nan if z is None else float(z)).to_numpy(dtype=float); src[c] = c; continue
152	        levels = sorted({str(z) for z in vals if z is not None})
153	        if len(levels) > max_levels: continue
154	        for lv in levels:
155	            k = f"{c}={lv}"; out[k] = (vals.map(lambda z: None if z is None else str(z)) == lv).astype(float).to_numpy(); src[k] = c
156	    return pd.DataFrame(out), src

238	def metrics(T, keep, rows, tag, controls=True, draws=CONTROL_DRAWS):
239	    """Kept-vs-skipped metrics of a boolean keep mask over the rows `rows` of T (a subset of one split)."""
240	    keep = np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool)
241	    k = rows[keep[rows]]; s = rows[~keep[rows]]
242	    net, win = T.net, T.win
243	    nk, ns = len(k), len(s)
244	    m = dict(n=int(len(rows)), kept_n=int(nk), skipped_n=int(ns), kept_share=round(nk / len(rows), 4) if len(rows) else None,
245	             kept_net=round(float(net[k].sum()), 2), skipped_net=round(float(net[s].sum()), 2),
246	             kept_mean=round(float(net[k].mean()), 2) if nk else None, skipped_mean=round(float(net[s].mean()), 2) if ns else None,
247	             all_mean=round(float(net[rows].mean()), 2) if len(rows) else None,
248	             kept_win_rate=round(float(win[k].mean()), 4) if nk else None, skipped_win_rate=round(float(win[s].mean()), 4) if ns else None,
249	             kept_pf=None, kept_t=None, diff=None, diff_top1_removed=None, kept_mean_slip3=None, kept_mean_slip8=None,
250	             loser_recall=None, loser_precision=None, winner_recall=None, winner_recall_weighted=None, top_decile_winners_skipped=None,
251	             kept_sessions=int(len(set(T.session[k].tolist()))), sign_blocks=None, perm_p=None, control_pct=None, control_p_beat=None)
252	    if nk:
253	        w_, l_ = net[k][net[k] > 0], net[k][net[k] <= 0]
254	        m["kept_pf"] = round(float(w_.sum() / -l_.sum()), 3) if len(l_) and l_.sum() else None
255	        m["kept_t"] = round(float(net[k].mean() / (net[k].std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(nk))), 2) if nk > 1 and net[k].std(ddof=1) else None
256	    if nk and ns:
257	        m["diff"] = round(float(net[k].mean() - net[s].mean()), 2)
258	        # slippage moves every trade's net by the same amount, so the kept-vs-skipped difference is invariant; what a marginal
259	        # gate must survive is the kept book's own expectancy at 3 / 8 pts per side
260	        for sl_ in (3.0, 8.0): m[f"kept_mean_slip{int(sl_)}"] = round(float(T.net_slip[sl_][k].mean()), 2)
261	        top = np.quantile(net[rows], 0.99); kk, ss_ = k[net[k] < top], s[net[s] < top]
262	        m["diff_top1_removed"] = round(float(net[kk].mean() - net[ss_].mean()), 2) if len(kk) and len(ss_) else None
263	        L = ~win[rows]; W = win[rows]
264	        skp = ~keep[rows]
265	        m["loser_recall"] = round(float((skp & L).sum() / L.sum()), 4) if L.sum() else None
266	        m["loser_precision"] = round(float((skp & L).sum() / skp.sum()), 4) if skp.sum() else None
267	        m["winner_recall"] = round(float((~skp & W).sum() / W.sum()), 4) if W.sum() else None
268	        wn = net[rows]
269	        m["winner_recall_weighted"] = round(float(wn[~skp & W].sum() / wn[W].sum()), 4) if W.sum() and wn[W].sum() else None
270	        if W.sum():
271	            q = np.quantile(wn[W], 0.9); big = W & (wn >= q)
272	            m["top_decile_winners_skipped"] = round(float((skp & big).sum() / big.sum()), 4) if big.sum() else None
273	        bl = T.block[rows]
274	        if (bl >= 0).all():
275	            m["sign_blocks"] = int(sum(1 for b in range(N_BLOCKS) if (keep[rows] & (bl == b)).sum() and (~keep[rows] & (bl == b)).sum()
276	                                      and net[rows][keep[rows] & (bl == b)].mean() > net[rows][~keep[rows] & (bl == b)].mean()))
277	        if controls:
278	            pp = fz_report.permutation_p(net[k].tolist(), net[s].tolist(), draws, SEED, tag)
279	            m["perm_p"] = pp["p"]
280	            rc = fz_report.random_control(_units(T, rows), _units(T, k, "SEL"), draws, SEED, tag)
281	            m["control_pct"], m["control_p_beat"], m["control_p50"] = rc["fz_pct"], rc["p_beat"], rc["p50"]
282	    return m

285	def session_vectors(T, keep, rows):
286	    """Per active session (sessions with a unit among rows): kept sum / n, skipped sum / n, all sum / n."""
287	    keep = np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool)
288	    ses = T.session[rows]; net = T.net[rows]; kp = keep[rows]
289	    S = np.array(sorted(set(ses.tolist())))
290	    idx = np.searchsorted(S, ses)
291	    out = {}
292	    for name, msk in (("kept", kp), ("skipped", ~kp), ("all", np.ones(len(rows), dtype=bool))):
293	        out[name + "_sum"] = np.bincount(idx, weights=net * msk, minlength=len(S))
294	        out[name + "_n"] = np.bincount(idx, weights=msk.astype(float), minlength=len(S))
295	    out["sessions"] = S
296	    return out

320	def score_paths(T, paths, family, config, script=None, controls=False, threshold=None):
321	    """CPCV: score each of the 11 path masks (a path is a decision array over rows: booleans, or scores compared with
322	    `threshold` when given). Returns the per-path metrics and the distribution of diff (median, 5th percentile, min) and of
323	    the control percentile when controls is set; every path is a ledger row of family '<family>/cpcv'."""
324	    out = []
325	    for p, arr in enumerate(paths):
326	        keep = np.asarray(arr) >= threshold if threshold is not None else np.asarray(arr).astype(bool)
327	        out.append(score(T, keep, f"{family}/cpcv", dict(config, path=p), script=script, controls=controls))
328	    d = np.array([x["diff"] if x["diff"] is not None else np.nan for x in out], dtype=float)
329	    res = dict(paths=len(out), diff_median=round(float(np.nanmedian(d)), 2), diff_p5=round(float(np.nanquantile(d, 0.05)), 2),
330	               diff_min=round(float(np.nanmin(d)), 2), diff_share_positive=round(float((d > 0).mean()), 3),
331	               kept_share_median=round(float(np.median([x["kept_share"] for x in out])), 4))
332	    if controls:
333	        c = np.array([x["control_pct"] if x["control_pct"] is not None else np.nan for x in out], dtype=float)
334	        res.update(control_pct_median=round(float(np.nanmedian(c)), 1), control_pct_p5=round(float(np.nanquantile(c, 0.05)), 1))
335	    return res, out

587	def go_no_go(res, tf, cpcv=None, pbo_value=None, dsr=None, spa_p=None, boot=None, null_tape=None, columns=None):
588	    """The pre-registered pass rule on a candidate's IS results. Returns (passed, {check: (ok, value)}).
589	
590	    Two items added 2026-09-29 12:55 UTC from the null_tapes_drift refuters (Judge 1's binding fix), both required for a pass:
591	      null_tape  the `checks` dict of studies/null_tapes_drift/tapes.py::null_tape_check(real_diff, tf, rules) (or of
592	                 null_tape_check_from_diffs for a candidate replayed on the certificate tapes some other way, e.g. an online
593	                 learner run on each tape's table): the real-tape kept-vs-skipped difference must exceed the gmm AND segment
594	                 tapes' 95th percentile and the session tapes must carry its sign in >= 75% of tapes. None -> the item fails as
595	                 "not run"; a string -> recorded as the reason and the item still fails (no candidate passes without the tapes).
596	      columns    the as-of columns the candidate reads; any TIME_PROXIES / NOT_FEATURES / label-prefixed name fails the item
597	                 "no_time_proxy_columns" (a rule on `sl` or `n_events_asof` is a calendar rule). None -> fails as "not declared".
598	    Before that date the function had neither item; every study that called it up to then recorded passed=False anyway."""
599	    ch = {}
600	    ch["kept_share>=20%"] = (res.get("kept_share") is not None and res["kept_share"] >= GO["kept_share_min"], res.get("kept_share"))
601	    ch[f"kept_n>={GO['kept_n_min'][tf]}"] = (res.get("kept_n", 0) >= GO["kept_n_min"][tf], res.get("kept_n"))
602	    ch["diff>0"] = (res.get("diff") is not None and res["diff"] > 0, res.get("diff"))
603	    ch["diff_top1_removed>0"] = (res.get("diff_top1_removed") is not None and res["diff_top1_removed"] > GO["top1_removed_diff_min"], res.get("diff_top1_removed"))
604	    ch["kept_mean_slip8>0"] = (res.get("kept_mean_slip8") is not None and res["kept_mean_slip8"] > GO["slip8_kept_mean_min"], res.get("kept_mean_slip8"))
605	    ch[f"sign_blocks>={GO['sign_blocks_min']}/12"] = (res.get("sign_blocks") is not None and res["sign_blocks"] >= GO["sign_blocks_min"], res.get("sign_blocks"))
606	    ch["control_pct>=95"] = (res.get("control_pct") is not None and res["control_pct"] >= GO["control_pct_min"], res.get("control_pct"))
607	    if cpcv is not None: ch["cpcv_p5_diff>0"] = (cpcv.get("diff_p5") is not None and cpcv["diff_p5"] > GO["cpcv_p5_diff_min"], cpcv.get("diff_p5"))
608	    if pbo_value is not None: ch["pbo<=0.2"] = (pbo_value <= GO["pbo_max"], pbo_value)
609	    if dsr is not None: ch["dsr_p<0.1"] = (dsr.get("p") is not None and dsr["p"] < GO["dsr_p_max"], dsr.get("p"))
610	    if spa_p is not None: ch["spa_p<=0.10"] = (spa_p <= GO["spa_p_max"], spa_p)
611	    if boot is not None: ch["boot_ci_excludes_0"] = (boot["diff_ci"][0] > 0, boot["diff_ci"])
612	    if isinstance(null_tape, dict) and null_tape:
613	        for k, v in null_tape.items(): ch[k if str(k).startswith("null_tape") else f"null_tape:{k}"] = (bool(v[0]), v[1]) if isinstance(v, (tuple, list)) else (bool(v), v)
614	    else:
615	        ch["null_tape:evaluated"] = (False, "not run" if null_tape is None else str(null_tape))
616	    if columns is None:
617	        ch["no_time_proxy_columns"] = (False, "columns not declared")
618	    else:
619	        bad = sorted(c for c in columns if c in TIME_PROXIES or c in NOT_FEATURES or str(c).startswith(LABEL_PREFIX))
620	        ch["no_time_proxy_columns"] = (not bad, bad if bad else sorted(set(columns)))
621	    return all(v[0] for v in ch.values()), ch

import json, sys, pickle, os
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0,'.'); sys.path.insert(0,'studies/online_learner')
import harness as H
rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open('ledger/trials.jsonl') if l.strip()]
onl=[r for r in rows if r['family'].startswith('online')]
print('online* ledger rows', len(onl))
from collections import Counter
print('script/sha by tf:', Counter((r['tf'], r['script'], r['script_sha']) for r in onl))
print('current run_online.py sha', H.file_sha('studies/online_learner/run_online.py'), 'finalize sha', H.file_sha('studies/online_learner/finalize.py'))
print('time range by tf:', {tf:(min(r['at'] for r in onl if r['tf']==tf), max(r['at'] for r in onl if r['tf']==tf)) for tf in ('minute','5minute')})
ids=Counter(r['id'] for r in onl); print('dup ids', [k for k,v in ids.items() if v>1])
# reproduce the top row
T=H.load('minute'); rows_is=np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
r=[x for x in onl if x['id']=='19f7ff81224bafa0'][0]
sc=[json.loads(l) for l in open('studies/online_learner/results/minute/scores.jsonl') if l.strip()]
s=[x for x in sc if x['id']=='19f7ff81224bafa0'][0]
J=pickle.load(open(os.path.join('studies/online_learner/results/minute/jobs', s['job']+'.pkl'),'rb'))
h=next(x for x in J['heads'] if x['head']==s['head'])
keep=np.zeros(T.n,bool); keep[J['rows']]=h['keep']
m=H.metrics(T,keep,rows_is,'refuter',controls=False)
print('ledger:', {k:r[k] for k in ('kept_n','kept_share','kept_mean','skipped_mean','diff','diff_top1_removed','kept_pf','sign_blocks','kept_mean_slip8','control_pct','perm_p')})
print('recomp:', {k:m[k] for k in ('kept_n','kept_share','kept_mean','skipped_mean','diff','diff_top1_removed','kept_pf','sign_blocks','kept_mean_slip8')})
print('config', r['config'])
# kept trades: where in time are they? 
kt=np.flatnonzero(keep); print('kept by year', Counter(str(T.day[i])[:4] for i in kt)); print('kept hour_bin', Counter(T.F.hour_bin.iloc[kt].astype(str))); print('kept dir', Counter(T.F.dir.iloc[kt].astype(str)))
print('kept nets top5', sorted(T.net[kt])[-5:], 'sum', T.net[kt].sum())
EOF

content.description: fz_v3/out/harness.py: the single evaluator. Every gate candidate goes through score(); kept-vs-skipped expectancy, session-matched random control (fz_report.random_control), permutation p (fz_report.permutation_p), CPCV 11 paths, go/no-go rule (PBO <= 0.2, CPCV p5 diff > 0, DSR p < 0.1, kept share >= 20%, kept n >= 300/80, top-1%-removed value > 0, slippage 8 pts survival). Break tests (BDE CUSUM, Chow) as pre-registration.

Result: the frozen shortlist is EMPTY on both timeframes (0 clusters pass MDA mean > std AND stability); full-model ceiling AUC 0.59 (1m) / 0.50 (5m). Verified by two refuters, repaired once (registration note corrected to "frozen before the phase-3 gate studies"), rechecked.

content.description: H1 what ST7/ST8 skip (precision/recall as loser filter, big winners); H2 regime grid; H3 visibly-high-volume reaction; H4 level respect vs break; H5 depth-3 tree + greedy rule list + GBM ceiling. All IS, via score(), every trial in the ledger.
